K=1 QUESTIONS NEVER RUN THE GRAPH (LayaEngine.askChoice): a 1-option choice is answered as exactly {option: 1.0} without a forward pass. Reason: the official exporter traces the act-head's `p.size(-1) >= 2` TopK branch as a Python constant (TracerWarning visible in the export log), so the exported graph raises 'TopK k argument [2] should not be greater than specified axis dim value [1]' for any 1-marker input — a real-loop bucket with exactly one candidate (and a single-bucket state) hits this. Mathematically faithful: softmax over one logit is exactly 1.0; the decision is unaffected. Upstream export limitation, recorded here.

ShadowRouter bookkeeping corrections found by the gates: snapshot.sampled now comes from an unbounded counter (the tracked-jobs deque is bounded at 8 and undercounted long runs); MEASURED laya latencies are now recorded for EVERY completed shadow decision (previously only when a row enriched, so a missed run reported no latency — Gate 8.4's 'measured latency recorded' needs it regardless); Snapshot.lastFailure carries the last shadow failure's class+message (the failure path is swallow-by-design, so run reports can show WHY).

Harness test-infra (NOT loop/product changes): WARMUP_WAIT_MS 60s -> 120s (the FIRST page load after a fresh emulator boot measures ~90s before the WebView exposes its content tree; 60s starved the runbook) and an adb-settable settleMs extra for the loop's page-settle pacing (default = the loop's own 700ms default; used to probe whether pacing could close the Gate 8.4 coverage race — it cannot, because the row writes before the settle). Gate 8.4 also needs the browser TRULY dead before a run's cold-start (killBackgroundProcesses does not kill on modern Android; a surviving browser swallows the VIEW intent via onNewIntent and never navigates) — runbook note recorded in gate84 evidence.

Reference-vector fixture notes (tools/laya_reference.py): agent.predict takes the USER question format ({type, instructions, criteria}) — _to_internal maps it to the {t, ins, crit} form the fixture stores, so the recorded sequences are the internal form build_sequence consumes; a noul answer carries only 'noul' (p_true), from which [p_false, p_true] is reconstructed for the drift record. The fixture's probabilities are POSITIONALLY aligned with optionIds (element-stage ids are node ids, crit keys are labels — only arity asserts equal; bucket-stage ids ARE the labels).
